Q1.setting: the putting application's context option: MQPMO_DEFAULT_CONTEXT, assumed when no context option is given, has the queue manager set PutDate and PutTime (so do MQPMO_PASS_IDENTITY_CONTEXT and MQPMO_SET_IDENTITY_CONTEXT); MQPMO_SET_ALL_CONTEXT lets the application supply its own values and MQPMO_NO_CONTEXT leaves them blank

evidence.quote: PutTime (MQCHAR8) This is the time when the message was put, and is part of the origin context of the message.

MQPMO_DEFAULT_CONTEXT The message is to have default context information associated with it, for both identity and origin. The queue manager sets the context fields in the message descriptor as follows:
PutDate Set to the date when message is put. PutTime Set to the time when message is put.
You can specify only one of the MQPMO_*_CONTEXT context options. If you specify none, MQPMO_DEFAULT_CONTEXT is assumed.
MQPMO_SET_ALL_CONTEXT The message is to have context information associated with it. The application specifies the identity, origin, and user context in the MQMD structure.
MQPMO_NO_CONTEXT Both identity and origin context are set to indicate no context.
HH hours (00 through 23) MM minutes (00 through 59) SS seconds (00 through 59; see note) T tenths of a second (0 through 9) H hundredths of a second (0 through 9)
Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) is used for the PutDate and PutTime fields, subject to the system clock being set accurately to GMT.
The message channel agent (MCA) never alters message context. MCAs that receive messages from remote queue managers use the context option MQPMO_SET_ALL_CONTEXT on the MQPUT or MQPUT1 call.

Q1.note: With default context, which applies when the putting application names no context option, the queue manager stamps the time it processes the put (for a put inside a unit of work, the put and not the commit). Coded 'by configuration', on by default, because the putting application's context option decides: MQPMO_SET_ALL_CONTEXT, which needs set-all authority, supplies the application's own date and time, and MQPMO_NO_CONTEXT leaves both blank. Channels pass the context on unchanged (the receiving end puts with MQPMO_SET_ALL_CONTEXT), so a message that crossed queue managers carries the time it was put at the first queue manager, on that queue manager's clock. The publication property MQPubTime is an optional timestamp set by the publisher, not by the queue manager.

Q5.field: MQMD Expiry: the remaining lifetime at MQGET

evidence.quote: Expiry (MQLONG) This is a period of time expressed in tenths of a second, set by the application that puts the message.
The value is decremented to reflect the time that the message spends on the destination queue, and also on any intermediate transmission queues if the put is to a remote queue.
When the message is retrieved by an application using the MQGET call, the Expiry field represents the expiry time that still remains.
However, the expiration time is treated as approximate, and the value need not be decremented to reflect small time intervals.

Q5.note: Coded as the MQTT 5.0 expiry was: a getter that knows the Expiry the putting application set (agreed with it, or repeated by it in a message property) obtains the message's time on the queue, and on any transmission queues, as the difference, in tenths of a second. The documentation calls the decrement approximate and says small intervals need not be counted, so short stays may not show. Only messages put with an expiry carry it (MQEI_UNLIMITED otherwise), and a queue's or topic's CAPEXPRY can lower the expiry set at the put.

Q6.what: Application activity trace: a PCF record of every MQI call an application makes (MQGET, MQPUT, the message-consumer callbacks), with the operation's time; at trace level 2 and above each operation carries HighResTime in microseconds. Enabled by the ACTVTRC queue manager attribute, MQCONNX options or the mqat.ini stanza; written to SYSTEM.ADMIN.TRACE.ACTIVITY.QUEUE or system topics. Not available on z/OS.

evidence.quote: Application activity trace produces detailed information about the behavior of applications connected to a queue manager.
It also shows the sequence of MQI calls issued by an application.
HighResTime Description: Time of operation in microseconds since midnight, January 1st 1970 (UTC)
To configure central collection of application activity trace information, you set the ACTVTRC queue manager attribute.
Note that activity trace is not supported by IBM MQ for z/OS.

evidence.quote: Read ahead allows messages to be sent to a client without an application having to request them.
When read ahead is enabled, messages are sent to a memory buffer on the client called the read ahead buffer.
The client periodically updates the server with information about the amount of data it has consumed.

read_back.question: Q7
read_back.read: Read ahead sends messages to a memory buffer on the client without the application requesting them, the client periodically tells the server how much data it has consumed, and the client enables it only when stated conditions are met, so the server's sending ahead is paced by a credit counted in data.
